lead: If they’re happy, you’re happier. Valencia is a flat city with beaches, nature and activities for every taste and age. The perfect family destination on the Mediterranean.

Valencia has everything a family needs: short distances, easy transport, a completely flat city, a six-month beach season and a range of activities that runs from Europe’s largest aquarium to a giant playground right in the centre. And all of it in a mild Mediterranean climate for practically the whole year.
Here are the 12 best things to do in Valencia with children, with information on prices, recommended ages and the detail that makes each visit special.

items.title: Oceanogràfic
items.body: Europe’s largest aquarium, with more than 45,000 specimens of 500 marine species. The underwater tunnel with sharks and rays, the dolphinarium and the aviary in a 27-metre sphere are the star moments of the visit. Book in advance: it sells out at weekends.
facts: From €39.45 adult · From €29.65 child · Free for under-3s

items.title: BIOPARC Valencia
items.body: A new-generation zoo where the barriers are practically invisible and the animals roam spaces that recreate their African habitats. Elephants, lions, gorillas, hippos, lemurs and more than 6,000 animals of 150 species. One of the best animal parks in Europe.
facts: Parque de Cabecera · Av. Pío Baroja
From €32.50 adult · From €24 child · Free for under-3s

items.title: Gulliver Park
items.body: Valencia’s most original playground: a 70-metre-long figure of Gulliver lying down, turned into a play park. His body is full of slides of all sizes, climbing ropes and ladders. Children become the inhabitants of Lilliput. Completely free entry.
facts: Turia Gardens · Between the Puente del Ángel and the Pont del Regne
Free · Open access all year round

items.title: Museu de les Ciències
items.body: Under the motto “forbidden not to touch”, the largest interactive science and technology museum in the Valencian Community. The Espai dels Xiquets is designed especially for children aged 3 to 8 with activities on the senses, water and animals. The Science Theatre puts on shows included in the admission.

items.title: L’Albufera Natural Park
items.body: An ecological paradise ten kilometres from the centre with traditional boat trips on the lake, rice fields, dunes and wetland wildlife. The place where Valencian paella was born. Sunsets from the boat are a magical experience for the whole family. Buses 24 and 25 leave from the centre and are free with the Tourist Card.
facts: 10 km from the centre · Bus 24 and 25
Boat trip: from €8 · Boat + paella pack from €26

items.title: Turia Gardens and cycle route
items.body: Valencia’s longest linear park, 9 kilometres without cars along the old riverbed. Perfect for riding as a family, with the Bioparc and the Gulliver Park on the way and the City of Arts at the end. Family bike hire is available, with seat options for the little ones.
facts: 9 km · From the Parque de Cabecera to the CAC

items.title: Indiana Jones and the Holy Grail tour
items.body: A two-hour tour of the historic centre with Indiana Jones himself as your guide. Games, riddles and legends about the Holy Grail kept in Valencia Cathedral. A hugely fun way for children to discover the city’s history without getting bored. Highly recommended for families with children aged 6 and over.

items.title: Iluziona Museum
items.body: A museum of optical illusions and interactive experiences that plays with visual perception. Settings inspired by legends, films, natural landscapes and Valencian traditions. It also includes a virtual reality experience with dinosaurs and a motocross circuit. Perfect for families with children who love photos and visual challenges.

items.title: Fallero Museum
items.body: The museum where the ninots pardoned from Las Fallas since 1934 are kept. The caricatures and prize-winning posters are a very fun way to learn about Valencian history and culture. Admission is included in the Valencia Tourist Card. It can easily be visited alongside the Gulliver Park, as they are very close.
facts: Plaza Monteolivete · Near the Gulliver Park
Free with the Tourist Card · Admission: €2

items.title: Ratoncito Pérez’s Warehouse
items.body: A 45-minute theatrical guided visit designed especially for the youngest members of the family. Children learn about dental hygiene, geography and music as they discover the magical warehouse where Ratoncito Pérez keeps the teeth. An experience full of art, affection and imagination that little ones won’t forget.

items.title: Urban beaches: Malvarrosa and Cabanyal
items.body: More than 4 kilometres of Blue Flag urban beaches easily reached by metro or bus from the centre. Malvarrosa beach is the busiest and liveliest, with restaurants right on the seafront. El Cabanyal has a more seafaring atmosphere and districts with unique Modernista architecture. In summer, the Mediterranean reaches 26 °C.
facts: Maritime Villages · Metro L3 or bus
Free · Metro or bus from the centre

items.title: The Red Bus tourist bus
items.body: The classic open-top double-decker tourist bus with stops at Valencia’s main points of interest. Children especially enjoy the upper deck and being able to hop on and off as often as they like for 24 or 48 hours. It is also a good way to get your bearings in the city on your first day. Discount with the Tourist Card.
facts: From €26 adult · From €13 child (5–15 years) · Free for under-4s

items.title: Getting around as a family
items.body: The metro and the bus are easy and affordable. The Tourist Card includes unlimited transport and the city is completely flat, ideal for pushchairs and wheelchairs.

items.title: Best time to visit
items.body: Valencia has beach weather from April to October. In winter, the mild climate (10–18 °C) lets you visit the city without heavy coats. Avoid August if you are sensitive to heat.

items.title: Pushchairs and accessibility
items.body: The city is mostly flat. The biggest museums and the Turia Gardens are fully accessible with pushchairs and wheelchairs.

items.title: Valencia Tourist Card
items.body: For families with children it is especially good value: unlimited transport, free municipal museums and up to 15% off the Oceanogràfic and the CAC.

blocks.title: The most important things before travelling to Valencia with children
items: Book the Oceanogràfic and BIOPARC online in advance to avoid queues
The Gulliver Park and the Turia Gardens are free and perfect for resting between visits
The 72-hour Tourist Card includes transport and discounts at the CAC and BIOPARC
Children under 3 enter the Oceanogràfic and BIOPARC free
Bus 24 and 25 go to the Albufera and are free with the Tourist Card
The Indiana Jones tour is one of the best cultural activities for children aged 6 and over
